pitch_hook: US beekeepers lost 56% of their hives in 2024-25, the most their national survey has ever recorded. Over half of the native bee species scientists checked are declining. Maya is seven and wants to help, but she won't read a pamphlet. So we put a bee in her ear.

objects.label: native_flower
objects.name: Common sunflower (Helianthus annuus, native to North America)
objects.buy_or_print: Print card: one big sunflower head, front-on, filling the frame, on a plain sky or dark background. Optional real prop: a grocery sunflower bouquet (Trader Joe's, Safeway) on the table next to the card.
objects.camera_notes: Yellow petal ring around a dark brown disk: a bold, symmetric, high-contrast circle that reads from across a room. Only yellow-and-round card at the booth.
objects.dataset_class: Open Images 'Sunflower'; ImageNet 'daisy' (closest); COCO 'potted plant' / 'vase' if a real bouquet is used
objects.theme: Pollination: some scientists estimate one in three bites of food exists because of animal pollinators

objects.label: honey_jar
objects.name: Store honey (honey bear squeeze bottle)
objects.buy_or_print: Print card: a backlit amber honey bear bottle (or a glass jar with a honey dipper) on white. Optional real prop: any grocery honey bear in front of the card.
objects.camera_notes: Glowing amber bear silhouette with a cap: a warm orange-gold blob with a unique outline. Sits two stations from the sunflower, so the two yellows rarely share a frame.
objects.dataset_class: COCO 'bottle' (bear shape also resembles 'teddy bear'); ImageNet 'water bottle'
objects.theme: Honey takes up to two million flower visits per pound; never leave store honey out for bees (foulbrood)

objects.label: bug_spray
objects.name: Bug spray can (aerosol insecticide)
objects.buy_or_print: Print card: a generic aerosol can (no brand logo) with a red X or a mist cloud, on a plain background. Avoid yellow cans. Kid-safe: no real insecticide at the booth.
objects.camera_notes: Tall narrow metal cylinder with a cap and spray nozzle: a vertical silhouette nothing else has. A big red X adds a strong color cue.
objects.theme: Pesticides: the twist station. Oral insecticide toxicity loading on US farmland rose about 48-fold from 1992 to 2014, mostly from neonicotinoids

objects.label: bee_hotel
objects.name: Bee hotel (wood house with tube nests for mason and leafcutter bees)
objects.buy_or_print: Print card: close photo of a wooden bee hotel face, rows of bamboo tubes and drilled holes, ideally with a little roof. Optional real prop: a store bee house.
objects.camera_notes: A grid of many small dark round holes in pale wood: a dense, high-contrast texture unlike any other card. Fill the card with the hole pattern.
objects.dataset_class: No COCO class; ImageNet 'honeycomb' (closest texture), sometimes 'birdhouse'
objects.theme: Native bees: over half of assessed species declining, nearly one in four imperiled

objects.label: pebble_dish
objects.name: Bee water dish (shallow bowl of pebbles and water)
objects.buy_or_print: Print card: top-down photo of a bright blue or white shallow bowl filled with grey pebbles, water glinting between them. Optional real prop: bowl + vase pebbles from a grocery floral aisle or dollar store.
objects.camera_notes: A round bowl seen from above, full of speckled pebbles: circle-in-circle with busy grey texture. Blue bowl color is unique at the booth.
objects.theme: Bees need water and can't swim; water bees carry about eighty percent of their weight in water to cool the hive

objects.label: beehive
objects.name: Honey bee hive (white stacked Langstroth boxes)
objects.buy_or_print: Print card: a white stacked Langstroth hive (two or three boxes and a lid) in green grass, hive filling most of the card.
objects.camera_notes: Tall stack of plain white rectangles with a dark entrance slot at the bottom, on green: blocky white-on-green, unlike every other card.
objects.dataset_class: ImageNet 'apiary, bee house'; no COCO class
objects.theme: Honey bee colony losses: about four in ten last year, more than half the year before; Varroa mites spreading viruses are a leading cause

lines.text: Hey, I'm Beeswax, your bee assistant. Fuzzy, grumpy, and living in your ear now.
We're out in nature. Let's see what it has for bees. Walk up to something and look down at it.
Bee fact found! Would you like to learn more?

lines.label: native_flower
lines.text: This is a sunflower. It grew wild in North America first.

lines.label: native_flower
lines.text: Some scientists think one in three bites you eat is thanks to pollinators like me.

lines.label: native_flower
lines.text: Now go to your next adventure. One big step to your left.

lines.label: honey_jar
lines.text: This is honey. One pound can take up to two million flower visits.

lines.label: honey_jar
lines.text: Never leave store honey out for bees. It can carry a bee germ. Fine on your toast.

lines.label: honey_jar
lines.text: Next adventure: one more step to your left. Brace yourself.

lines.label: bug_spray
lines.text: This is bug spray. Bees carry it home to the babies.

lines.label: bug_spray
lines.text: One study: US farmland got about forty-eight times more toxic for insects to eat in twenty-two years.

lines.label: bug_spray
lines.text: Ugh. Get away from that can. Your next adventure is one step to your left.

lines.label: bee_hotel
lines.text: This is a bee hotel, a home for wild bees.

lines.label: bee_hotel
lines.text: Of the kinds scientists checked, over half are shrinking. Nearly one in four is in danger.

lines.label: bee_hotel
lines.text: Thirsty? Your next adventure is one step to your left.

lines.label: pebble_dish
lines.text: This is a bee water dish. Bees can't swim. Pebbles are our landing pads.

lines.label: pebble_dish
lines.text: Hot day? Water bees haul home about eighty percent of their weight in water.

lines.label: pebble_dish
lines.text: Last adventure. One step to your left. It's the big one.

lines.label: beehive
lines.text: This is a beehive. Last year, US beekeepers lost about four in ten hives.

lines.label: beehive
lines.text: The year before? More than half. Mites spreading bee germs are a big reason.
A little to your left.
A little to your right.
Closer. Bees are small. So are my eyes.
Look down a little. Like you're reading the label.
Hey! Where'd you go? I'm a bee, not a bloodhound. Find the next picture.
Left. Your other left.
Fine. Saving it for later.
Your call. I'll be right here. Grumbling.
Buzzing off! I'll be quiet. Mostly. Look at something when you miss me.
Nothing? I'll take that as a yes.
Nothing? I'll save it for later.
Slow day. Walk up to a picture and look down at it. I'll do the rest.
You found them all! Bee scout badge earned. Now go tell a human. Bees can't text.
Six for six! You're an official bee scout. I'm not crying. It's pollen.
Your jobs this week: plant one flower, put out a pebble dish, and ask grown-ups to skip the bug spray.
Bonus job: leave a patch of bare dirt. Most wild bees nest underground. Now go tell a friend.

sources.claim: Common sunflower is native to the western US and parts of Mexico; the center disk has more than 50 flowers; Helianthus supports specialist bees

USDA: 'Some scientists estimate that one out of every three bites of food we eat exists because of animal pollinators'; three-fourths of flowering plants and about 35% of food crops depend on animal pollinators
Colorado State University Extension: 'it can require up to 2 million flower visits to produce 1 pound of honey'
Never feed honey from outside sources to bees; American foulbrood spores survive for decades; affects bee larvae only
Foulbrood is harmless to people and the honey remains safe food
Pesticide residue on flowers is carried home in pollen and nectar to the brood

DiBartolomeis et al. 2019 (PLOS ONE): 48-fold increase in acute insecticide toxicity loading for oral exposure (4-fold for contact) on US agricultural land, 1992 to 2014; neonicotinoids are 61 to nearly 99% of 2014 loading; honey bee toxicity used as a proxy for insects; a screening metric, not a direct measure of harm
Xerces: 70% of native bees nest in the ground, 30% in cavities such as leafcutter and mason bees; keep insect hotels clean, they can spread disease and mites
Center for Biological Diversity 2017: of 1,437 North American and Hawaiian native bee species with sufficient data, more than half (749) are declining and 347 (nearly one in four) are imperiled
USGS: over 20,000 known bee species worldwide; 4,000 native to the United States
Bees can't swim and need gravel or a landing spot to drink; they spread water and fan to cool the hive
Water-collecting bees 'return carrying some 80 percent of their weight in water' when cooling an overheated hive (Ostwald, Smith and Seeley 2016)
US managed honey bee colonies: 39.9% annual loss April 2025 to April 2026 (winter 30.3%); 55.6% in 2024-25 and 55.1% in 2023-24; pressures named are parasites and poor forage
2024-25: US beekeepers lost an estimated 55.6% of managed colonies, the highest the national survey has recorded (pitch hook)
USDA ARS: viruses spread by miticide-resistant Varroa mites are the likely end-stage cause of the 2025 commercial colony collapses; nutritional stress and agrochemicals may also have played roles
USFWS: rusty patched bumble bee abundance plummeted 87% since the late 1990s; advice: plant native flowers blooming spring through fall, limit or avoid pesticides (backup stat, not in a line)
Plant native flowers that bloom spring to fall; small spaces count; avoid pesticides (finale actions)
